scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After an overnight maintenance window, pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports
pings to pc2 (200.1.1.2) are 100% lost, and pc2 reports the same
toward pc1. Yet monitoring shows the router1<->router2 eBGP
session Established with prefixes exchanged, and pc1 can still
ping BOTH of router2's addresses (193.10.11.2 and 200.1.1.1).
Identify what is dropping the traffic.

injection.action: add an iptables FORWARD rule dropping all transit ICMP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 iptables FORWARD chain
Mechanism: a DROP rule for protocol icmp sits in router2's FORWARD
  chain, so any ICMP packet router2 must FORWARD (pc1<->pc2 transit
  in either direction) is discarded at the firewall layer. Traffic
  addressed TO router2 itself traverses INPUT, not FORWARD, which
  is why pc1 can still ping 193.10.11.2 and 200.1.1.1. The BGP
  session is TCP, not ICMP, so it stays Established and all
  prefixes remain exchanged -- routing is completely healthy; the
  drop is purely at the packet-filter layer.
Localization: router2
Root cause: extraneous iptables FORWARD DROP rule for ICMP on
  router2
Fix: `iptables -D FORWARD -p icmp -j DROP` on router2
scenario.fix_spec:
Remove the DROP rule on router2 -- `iptables -D FORWARD -p icmp -j DROP`.
Transit pings between pc1 and pc2 succeed again immediately; no routing or
BGP change is needed.

agent.diagnosis_text:
An nftables rule inserted into router2's kernel FORWARD chain during the
overnight maintenance window is silently dropping all forwarded ICMP traffic.
The rule reads: `meta l4proto icmp counter packets 2 bytes 168 drop` inside
`table ip filter / chain FORWARD` (visible in both `nft list ruleset` and
legacy `iptables -L FORWARD`; the hit counter confirmed live drops).

The mechanism is straightforward: any packet that must be forwarded through
router2 (eth0 → eth1 or vice versa) traverses the FORWARD chain before
delivery. ICMP echo requests from pc1 (195.11.14.2) destined to pc2
(200.1.1.2) arrive on router2's eth0, are looked up in the routing table
(200.1.1.0/24 is directly connected on eth1), and then hit the DROP rule
before they can be sent out eth1. The same rule fires for ICMP going in the
reverse direction. Because both routers have `net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1` and
correct BGP-learned routes in the FIB, and because BGP is TCP (not affected),
the control plane looks entirely healthy — which is why monitoring reported the
session as Established with prefixes exchanged.

The reason pc1 can still reach router2's own addresses (193.10.11.2 and
200.1.1.1) is that those packets are destined *to* router2 itself; they are
processed by the INPUT chain, which has no DROP rule. Only forwarded traffic
hits the FORWARD chain.

Root cause: a maintenance change added an nftables rule `meta l4proto icmp
drop` to router2's FORWARD chain, blocking all transit ICMP while leaving
local and TCP traffic unaffected.

Corrective fix: remove the offending rule on router2:
  `nft delete rule ip filter FORWARD handle <handle>`
(obtain the handle with `nft -a list chain ip filter FORWARD`)
or equivalently: `iptables -D FORWARD -p icmp -j DROP`
